standard_prerequisites.name: A normal scheme whose quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components is a disjoint union of normal integral schemes, cited from the properties chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Decomposes the preimage of an affine open into finitely many normal integral pieces and gives the global conclusion.

standard_prerequisites.name: The compatibility of normalization with disjoint unions, established by a previous card of this lane, and the description of the normalization by integral closures
standard_prerequisites.use: Splits the normalization over the affine open into the normalizations in the individual pieces.

standard_prerequisites.name: The ring of global functions of a normal integral affine scheme is a normal domain, and the integral closure of a ring in a normal domain is a normal domain
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that each piece of the normalization is again a normal integral scheme.

core_obligations: Work over an affine open: take an affine open of the base, let the preimage of it in the source be V, and use compatibility of normalization with localization to identify the preimage in the normalization with the normalization of that affine open in V (proof lines 14182-14186).

Decompose the source: the preimage is quasi-compact and hence has finitely many irreducible components by hypothesis, so it is a finite disjoint union of normal integral schemes, and by compatibility of normalization with disjoint unions the normalization over the affine open splits accordingly (proof lines 14187-14196).

Identify the pieces: each piece is the spectrum of the integral closure of the base ring in a normal domain, which is again a normal domain, so the normalization over the affine open is a finite union of normal integral schemes and hence normal (proof lines 14197-14207).

Conclude globally: since the normalization is covered by these opens it is normal, each of which is a finite disjoint union of irreducible schemes so that every quasi-compact open of the normalization has finitely many irreducible components, and therefore the normalization is a disjoint union of normal integral schemes; dominance and the bijection on irreducible components are read off from the description over each affine open, the latter completed by a topological argument the author omits (proof lines 14208-14218).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an affine open of the base, decompose the preimage of the source into finitely many normal integral pieces and split the normalization accordingly (proof lines 14182-14196).

Show each piece is normal via integral closures in normal domains, conclude normality and the disjoint-union structure globally, and read off dominance and the bijection of components (proof lines 14197-14218).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism from a normal source whose quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components, the normalization of the base in the source is a disjoint union of integral normal schemes and the structure morphism is dominant with a bijection on irreducible components (statement lines 14169-14180). The counted proof is a systematic local computation: over an affine open of the base it decomposes the preimage of the source into finitely many normal integral pieces, splits the normalization accordingly using compatibility with localization and with disjoint unions, identifies each piece as the spectrum of an integral closure inside a normal domain hence again a normal domain, and then assembles normality and the disjoint-union structure globally before reading off dominance and the component bijection (proof lines 14182-14218). It is H2: the local computation and the global assembly are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard normalization and integral closure statements.
